best_for: Fansubbers, translators and video editors who time subtitles to audio by hand and typeset styled ASS subtitles over video.
description:
Aegisub is a free subtitle editor from the Aegisub Team. It works mainly in the ASS format, but it also opens and saves other subtitle formats, from MPEG-4 Timed Text to MicroDVD, and reads and writes Unicode as well as older text encodings.

A translation assistant helps you turn a script into another language, with spell checking and a thesaurus at hand. Shift Times moves a whole script, or just the lines you pick, earlier or later when it is out of sync. The audio view has a spectrum mode, and a timing post-processor can tidy up your line timings for you. It also handles variable frame rate video and reads timecodes straight from Matroska files. If your PC crashes, autosave, backups and emergency saves help you keep your work.

points.title: Built for timing and typesetting
points.text: You time lines against the audio, check them in a real-time video preview, and style them with ASS override tags and visual typesetting tools. A resolution resampler helps when the video size changes.

points.title: Scripts and karaoke
points.text: Lua automation scripts add macros, and the Karaoke Templater builds syllable-timed effects. The manual covers both with tutorials.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: Aegisub costs nothing. The project site describes its licensing as BSD-style, and Flathub lists BSD-3-Clause, MIT and MPL-1.1 for the Flatpak.

points.title: Maintained by TypesettingTools
points.text: Development happens in the TypesettingTools repository on GitHub. Version 3.5.1, released October 17, 2026, fixed a startup crash on macOS 13 and Lua scripts that could not load native modules on Mac.

points.title: 64-bit only
points.text: Windows gets a 64-bit installer that installs for the whole machine, plus a portable zip on the project site. There is no 32-bit build. The Mac app has separate Intel and Apple silicon builds and needs macOS 13.

points.title: Linux is a community Flatpak
points.text: The project itself publishes only a source tarball for Linux. The Flatpak listed here, for x64 and Arm64, is a Flathub build that Flathub does not mark as verified.

points.title: Spell check and versions
points.text: The Windows install includes only the US English dictionary. The Windows listing keeps 6 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
